instructions.content: CloudWatch URLs use the URL fragment (#) for all navigation state; the fragment is interpreted by the browser-side SPA, and standard %XX encoding does not apply inside fragment values.
Identify the target page type first: Logs Insights, Alarm detail, or Metrics graph.
Gather parameters: region, log group name, time range, query or metric name.
Apply *XX encoding (asterisk plus uppercase hex) to value portions only; structural characters (~, (, ), ') stay literal.
Compose the URL using the template in references/encoding-reference.md.
Verify before use: timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC and the region appears in both the subdomain and the query string.
For alarms, navigate to the alarm detail page first: it shows the exact metric that triggered the alarm, which may be a Logs metric filter rather than a native AWS/Lambda metric.
NEVER use %XX percent-encoding inside CloudWatch fragment values; use *XX.
NEVER use epoch integers for the Logs Insights time range; use ISO 8601 UTC strings with *3a-encoded colons, include tz~'UTC and omit unit~'seconds.
NEVER navigate to the AWS/Lambda Errors metric to verify an alarm.
NEVER omit region= from the query string.
NEVER use local/BST time in alarm or metric URL time ranges; derive times from UTC event timestamps.
NEVER omit the time range from an alarm detail URL used as incident evidence; append ?~(timeRange~(startDate~'{start_iso}~endDate~'{end_iso})) bracketing the whole incident.
Do not use this skill when the target page is outside CloudWatch, because encoding rules differ per service.
Do not use this skill when only the AWS Console root URL or a service listing is needed, since no fragment encoding is required.
NEVER encode the structural characters ~, (, ) or ' in the fragment.
NEVER leave ?, = or & unencoded between path segments after the #; write them $3F, $3D and $26.
